questions.title: Write a pseudocode algorithm for a function called knn. (Q28, ITE 2025)

items.text: The K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN) algorithm is used to classify a new data point by comparing it to existing classified/labelled data points. It calculates the Euclidean distance between the new data point (shown as a question mark on the chart below) and every other point in the training data. It then counts the labels of the k closest points. The most common label among these neighbours is the predicted label assigned to the new point.

Refer to the Stimulus.

Write a pseudocode algorithm for a function called knn. It is passed:

• newPoint: the x and y coordinates of the point to classify as A, B, C or D

• tData: an array of x and y coordinates for all labelled points

• tLabels: an array of strings with the label A, B, C or D for each known point

• k: an integer

 

You may use the following pre-defined functions in your algorithm:

• distance(p1, p2): returns the Euclidian distance between two (x, y) points

• sort(pairlist): sorts an array of [distance, label] pairs in ascending order by distance

• mode(array): returns the label that occurs most frequently in an array

 

Your algorithm should return the predicted label for the new data point.

criteria.criterion:
Produces a substantially correct algorithm which:

• Accepts the correct parameters and returns the label

• Calculates distance between the test point and all training points

• Selects the k closest points

• Extracts labels and determines the most common label

• Uses provided helper functions appropriately and efficiently
Produces an algorithm which completes at least four of the listed steps with minor errors.
Produces an algorithm which completes at least three of the listed steps but contains errors.
Produces an algorithm which completes at least two of the listed steps but contains errors.
Produces an algorithm which attempts some of the listed steps, but with significant errors.
Makes an attempt at an algorithm which relates to the question.

markingGuidanceContentItem.text:
BEGIN knn(newPoint, tData, tLabels, k)

    distances = []

     FOR i = 0 TO length of tData STEP 1

         d = distance(newPoint, tData[i])

         append [d, tLabels[i]] to distances

     NEXT i

     distances = sort(distances)

 

     nearest = []

     FOR i = 0 TO k - 1 STEP 1

         append distances[i][1] to nearest

     NEXT i

 

     label = mode(nearest)

     RETURN label

END

 

The above pseudocode uses Python-like syntax to specify arrays as lists. There is no direction in course specifications, so given Python is now specified we presume such syntax is preferred or at least will be equally acceptable to HSC examiners.

items.text:
Answer the question in the spaces provided.

If you include diagrams in your answer, ensure they are clearly labelled.

Logic programming takes a very different approach to the imperative paradigm and object-oriented programming.

Describe TWO characteristics and advantages of the logic programming paradigm.

criteria.criterion: Describes TWO characteristics and advantages of the logic programming paradigm.
Describes ONE characteristic and advantage of the logic programming paradigm OR identifies TWO characteristics.
Identifies ONE characteristic of the logic programming paradigm.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Answers may include:

  • Logic programming takes a declarative approach to programming, as opposed to an imperative approach. This means that it focuses on describing what needs to be done, rather than how to do it. The programmer defines a set of rules to follow and the programming language automatically determines an appropriate solution - which may be more efficient than if a programmer manually specified the solution in an imperative language.

  • Logic based programming expresses solutions in mathematical logic, allowing programmers to express complex relationships, constraints, and dependencies in a way where the reasoning can be followed. This can improve debugging and traceability of the program.

  • Logic-based languages allow non-deterministic execution, meaning the order of the code does not matter. This allows programmers to focus on defining rules, relationships, and so fourth without having to be concerned about control flow.

For the imperative and object-oriented paradigm you may use pseudocode, for the logic paradigm use Prolog.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Imperative:

BEGIN

sum = 0

FOR i = 1 TO LEN(numberList)

sum = sum + numberList[i]

NEXT i

PRINT sum

END

 

 

Object Oriented:

class ArrayMath {

private -

listOfNumbers: array of integers

public -

setListOfNumbers(numberList):

listOfNumbers = numberList

sumListOfNumbers():

FOR i = 1 TO LEN(listOfNumbers)

sum = sum + numberList[i]

NEXT i

RETURN sum

}

calculateSum = ArrayMath()

calculateSum.setListOfNumbers = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

PRINT calculateSum.sumListOfNumbers()

 

Logic (Prolog):

sum([], 0).

 

sum([Head|Tail], Total):-

sum(Tail, X),

Total is X + Head.

 

sum([1,2,3,4,5],SumTotal).

questions.title: Programming Paradigms (Question 30, ITE 2020)

items.text: Outline TWO limitations of the imperative paradigm.

criteria.criterion: Outlines TWO limitations of the imperative paradigm.
Outlines ONE limitation or identifies TWO limitations of the imperative paradigm.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Answers could include:

● Difficulty solving certain types of problems. Many problems may not have definite answers (e.g.
understanding tone or sentiment in written text) whereas imperative languages were designed to
solve problems with clear answers, such as mathematical or arithmetical problems.

● The need to specify code for every individual process. Imperative languages require the
programmer to specify how the problem should be solved in all situations, which may be lengthy or
sometimes impossible depending on the problem being addressed.

● Difficulty of coding for variability. While imperative code can be reused many times throughout a
program, this requires effort from the programmer. Other paradigms have this inherently part of the
programming approach.

items.text:
The learning curve required to adopt a new programming language is one factor influencing programmer productivity. 

Discuss TWO other factors which influence the productivity of programmers and relate these to programming paradigms..

criteria.criterion: Discusses TWO other factors which influence the productivity of programmers and relates these to programming paradigms.
Discusses TWO other factors which influence the productivity of programmers.
Discusses ONE other factor which influences the productivity of programmers or identifies TWO factors.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Answers could include:

● Speed of code generation. The speed at which programmers can write code which performs the
required task in an elegant, efficient manner, is a valuable measure of productivity. Different
programming paradigms are suitable for different types of problems and influence how fast a
programmer might be able to code a solution.

● Approach to testing. Testing individual models of code, known as unit testing, greatly affects
productivity through being able to continuously, and often automatically, test modules of code as
they are written or modified. This is heavily influenced by the programming paradigm chosen - for
example, object-oriented programming encourages programmers to write self-contained classes
which makes for easier testing.

● Effect on maintenance. Locating sections of code to be modified, and then having the required skills to modify that code (depending on the language and paradigm used), can be a time consuming task and influences productivity. The paradigm chosen has a great impact upon this, such as object-oriented programming languages encouraging programmers to modularise their code.

● Efficiency of solution once coded. Different programming languages have different levels of
efficiency once coded. For example, imperative languages such as C are aligned closely with the
CPU and usually run very efficiently, compared with object-oriented languages which are more
abstracted - but often easier and more efficient for the programmer.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text: OOP enhances automation by organising code into reusable classes and methods, which improves structure and maintainability. For example, each ML model (e.g., linear regression, neural network) can be represented as a class with specific methods for training, predicting, and updating. This modular approach allows developers to automate tasks like data processing, training, and deploying models without rewriting code, making it easier to manage, extend, and debug. OOP also allows different model classes to inherit properties, reducing redundancy and ensuring consistency across models.

questions.title: Why are high-level languages like Python used more than low-level languages like assembly? (Question 24, CSSA 2021)

items.text: Explain why higher level languages such as Python, JavaScript and C++ are more commonly used to write software compared to lower level languages such as assembly language .

criteria.criterion: Clearly explains why higher level languages are used over lower level languages in modern software development.

languages in modern software development.

Identifies at least ONE relevant reason why higher level languages are used over
lower level languages in modern software development.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Higher level languages are more commonly used as the instructions, which are written in plain
English and require a translation process from source code to machine code as the CPU cannot
directly understand the higher level source code. Whilst this translation process does increase
response time, the power of modern CPUs mean that this extra time waiting almost never impacts the end user. Furthermore the potential performance gains of using assembler language are far
outweighed by the productivity gained by the programmer who will write substantially less code by
using in-built libraries, commands and functions present in higher level languages.

questions.title: Developing a Binary Puzzle Solver (Question 22, ITE 2014)

items.text:
A binary puzzle consists of a grid, and each cell in the grid can only contain a 0 or 1.

The example below shows a 6 × 6 grid. The player is given an incomplete grid and needs to complete the puzzle according to the following rules:

  • You are not allowed to have more than two adjacent squares with the same number.
  • Each row and column must contain the same number of 0s and 1s. In a 6 × 6 puzzle grid there must be three 0s and three 1s in each row and each column.
  • Each row must not be the same as any other row, and each column must not be the same as any other column.

 

You have been asked to write a program which will automatically solve a basic 6 × 6 binary puzzle.

  • Locate pairs of numbers. Since you cannot have more than two adjacent squares with the same number, you can put the other number either side (or above and below) those pairs.
  • Locate potential trios of numbers. You can use the middle number to break-up potential trios, which are not allowed (as you can only have two adjacent squares with the same number).
  • Complete rows and columns. There must be three 0s and three 1s in each row and column. If the row has one incomplete cell that you can determine what that cell should hold.

These steps may need to be repeated multiple times to complete the grid. You can assume that all puzzles are solvable by following the above steps.
A two-dimensional array has been selected to represent the binary puzzle grid within the program. Justify this decision.

criteria.criterion: Provides suitable justification for the use of a two-dimensional array to represent the puzzle grid.
Identifies a feature of a two dimensional array.

markingRubricContentItem.text: Two-dimensional arrays are suitable for storing and representing grid or tabular based data since they allow for data to be addressed using two subscripts or indexes which naturally correspond to the row and column of the grid. In the case of the binary puzzle, the entire puzzle is represented as a grid. By storing the data within a two dimensional array this allows for algorithms to later access elements in the grid for the purpose of solving the binary puzzle.

items.text: It has been suggested that the data within the grid could be represented as either integer or Boolean values. Recommend the most appropriate data type to be used.

criteria.criterion: Provides a suitable recommendation for the use of an integer or Boolean data type to represent data within the grid.
Identifies a feature of an integer or Boolean data type.

markingRubricContentItem.text: By definition, values within the binary puzzle can only be one of two values: 0 or 1. While an integer data type could be used to represent these values, given the inherent limitation towards only supporting two values it is more suitable to use a Boolean data type. This may also help to avoid programming errors in the future by limiting the values which can be represented within the grid to those two possible states. However, it should also be noted that a third value would be used in the grid: nil or empty, to represent a cell which has not been completed.

markingRubricContentItem.text: This line checks whether the contents of a given cell is the same as the adjacent cell on the right-hand side. It first checks that the cell is not empty – if it’s not, then it checks the contents of the cell and then the cell on the same row but at cell index + 1 (i.e. the cell on the adjacent right-hand side).

items.text: Explain the processing performed by lines 6 to 11.

criteria.criterion: Correctly identifies and explains the logic of lines 6 to 11.
Correctly identifies the purpose of lines 6 to 11.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Lines 6 to 11 will run if two adjacent cells with the same number are found. In this case, the rules of the puzzle specify that the cells surrounding those two cells should be completed with the different number (as you may not have more than two consecutive cells with the same number).
Lines 6 to 8 will check that the cell is not in the first column (to avoid an out of bounds exception). If it’s not, then it will fill the cell on the left-hand side with the different number.
Lines 9 to 11 will check that the cell is not in the last column (also to avoid an out of bounds exception). If it’s not, then it will fill the cell on the right-hand side of the pairs (i.e. 2 cells more than the current cell, to compensate for the pair on the right-hand side) with the different number.

questions.title: Evaluating Commercial vs Custom LMS Solutions (Question 31, ITE 2019)

items.text:
Your school is considering the implementation of a new online learning management system (LMS). You have the choice between purchasing a commercial product, which will mostly meet user needs, versus developing your own system from scratch, which should meet all needs.

Outline different factors the school should consider in choosing between the systems.

criteria.criterion: Outlines a variety of factors, showing an excellent understanding of the issues relevant to the scenario
Outlines a variety of factors
Outlines a factor OR identifies factors
Identifies a factor

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Needs: the commercial system will “mostly meet user needs”. The needs it will not meet need to be
clearly identified. Are they essential for the users? Are there workarounds? Does the developer of the commercial system plan to implement them in the future?

Cost: the commercial system will come with an up-front cost, and possible ongoing costs as well. What are these costs? How do these compare with the cost of developing the LMS from scratch?
Licensing considerations: are there licensing considerations for either option? For example some
server operating systems or software will require licenses. If the school is hosting the LMS on-site then this may add cost.

Expertise: does the expertise exist within the school to develop the LMS from scratch? Or will
someone need to be hired to build it? Learning Management Systems are complex programs and will require significant expertise and time to build.

Maintainability/updates: How will this work for either option? For the commercial product how often are updates released? Can the school control the timing of these updates? What is the process if the school wants new functionality? If the LMS is developed in-house will the original developers be available to add new features and implement updates?

Related software: Many LMS products also have apps for phones and tablets. Are these provided as part of the commercial product? Does the company keep them up to date? If the LMS is developed from scratch will apps be created as well for ease of access to course materials? Has this been budgeted?

questions.title: Compare and contrast sequential files with relative files. (Q28, ITE 2024)

items.text: Compare and contrast sequential files with relative files.

criteria.criterion: Compares and contrasts sequential AND relative files.
Provides features of sequential AND relative files.
Identifies a feature of sequential OR relative files.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
Sequential files:

  • Data is stored and accessed in a linear sequence, one line after another.

  • New items are appended to the end of the file.

  • To access a specific item, the file must be read sequentially from the beginning until the desired item is found.

  • Simple file structure and easy to implement.

Relative files:

  • Records (items) can be accessed directly using a unique key, allowing for random access. This is possible because each record is of a predefined length.

  • New records can be appended to the end or existing records can be updated without affecting the positions of other records.

  • Suitable for applications that require direct access to specific records, such as database management systems or indexing systems.

  • More complex file structure compared to sequential files.

The key differences relate to the item/record access and updating methods along with the complexity of the files.

questions.title: Design and Evaluation of a Secure Airline Booking System (Question 24, ITE 2018)

items.text:
Freefall Airlines is a major airline which is developing a new online booking system to  replace their existing system. This new system has a focus on being user-friendly – as the  old system was very cumbersome with a poor user interface. The system needs to have the  following workflow: 

  1. Users are presented with the Freefall Airlines home page, allowing them to select the  origin and destination of their travel, departure and return dates, and travel class. 
  2. The system queries the Freefall Airlines backend database, along with the database of  their codeshare partners*, to find suitable flights meeting the criteria, and presents these to the user in a list with prices. 
  3. The user can select the flight(s) to book and then proceed to payment. 
  4. Payment is submitted online via credit card. 
  5. The user is then shown a confirmation on screen and is emailed their flight itinerary  and receipt. 

* In addition to searching for available Freefall Airlines flights the airline also has  arrangements with other airlines (known as a codeshare partnership) allowing Freefall  Airlines passengers to be booked on flights operated by the other airlines. As such, the  system needs to interface with their codeshare partners booking systems to find potential  available flights on other airlines.
Recommend and justify a suitable software development approach, or combination of 4 approaches, for the development of this system

criteria.criterion: Recommends and justifies a suitable approach, or combination of  approaches, with direct reference to the scenario.
Recommends and justifies a suitable approach, or combination of  approaches.
Recommends a suitable approach, or combination of approaches,  with basic justification.
Describes a software development approach.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Sample answer: 

The structured approach with prototyping are the most suitable software development  approaches. 

A structured approach for the majority of the system is suitable because: • This is a large mission-critical system for Freefall Airlines being their booking  system. It is likely that if the system were to fail, have bugs, or experience an  unplanned outage it could cost the airline a substantial amount of money in lost  revenue.

• The system involves taking payment, potentially for large sums of money, from  customers – so it needs to be designed in a disciplined and organised way to  ensure that payments are processed correctly. 

• The system also needs to interface with the codeshare partners. Integrating this  system with multiple other systems, which are potentially completely different,  would be a complex task requiring this system to be built to interface with the  exact specifications of the other systems. 

A prototyping approach is also suitable for the development of the user interface for  this system. Freefall Airlines want this system to be user-friendly, improving upon  their old system. Given that it is difficult to quantify user-friendliness in a structured  approach’s design specifications using prototyping provides a good way to iterate the  design of the user interface and validate/test with users prior to committing to a final  design. 

An agile approach is unsuitable as, due to the large size and scale of this system, the  lack of formal specifications and documentation when completing an agile project  would not be suitable. 

Rapid application development is unsuitable as this is a large multi-user network based system where aspects such as performance are important. Additionally, it likely  needs to be completely written custom and cannot use existing modules of code. 

The end user approach is unsuitable as the complexity of the project requires  specialised development skills.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
1. Slow internet access. Some users will be accessing the booking system on slow internet

items.text: The developers have determined that the Confirmed Bookings data store should be a random access file, not sequential file. Justify this decision.

criteria.criterion: Shows an excellent understanding of random access files, sequential files and the scenario
Identifies a feature of random access files or sequential files

markingRubricContentItem.text:
The Confirmed Bookings data store is likely to be large and contain many records, possibly even millions of them. The use cases for the data store, according to the DFD, are writing new records when a flight is booked, and reading them when the passenger checks in. For writing new records, it wouldn’t matter if the file was sequential or random access. For a sequential file, the new record could just be appended to the end of the file. For random access the data could also be written to the end.

However, for retrieving booking details, a random access file makes much more sense because if the booking reference can be used as a key then the record can be directly retrieved from the file, without the need to read any other records. This would be much faster, particularly as the data store will be large. If it was a sequential file then all records would need to be read until the particular record was found. Given the number of flights and passengers this would be a bottleneck on the system.

questions.title: Evaluating Custom Development vs Existing Solutions for Mining Data Software (Question 25, ITE 2020)

items.text:
A mining company needs new software to store information about their drilling tests. The information includes location data, depth, chemical analysis and high-resolution imagery. The software also needs to perform complex calculations to determine the viability of mining at each test site.

The company is weighing up whether they should develop their own software from scratch, or whether they can use existing software such as a database program.

Describe issues the mining company should consider when making this decision.

criteria.criterion: Describes relevant issues showing an excellent understanding of the scenario and issues relevant to the proposed solution
Describes relevant issues showing a good understanding of the scenario and issues relevant to the proposed solution
Describes a relevant issue
Identifies an issue

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Issues to consider:

● Customisation of existing software. Is it possible to develop this software using an existing
database program? Location data, depth, chemical analysis and imagery could be fields in a
database. A database should have the ability to add custom code, so the complex viability
calculations should be able to be implemented. There would be some unneeded overheads in an
existing database program, so it would use more space and resources than a program developed
from scratch.

● Cost effectiveness. The company would need to weigh up the cost of the database software vs
developing from scratch. An existing database would cost money, but less development time than a program developed from scratch.

● Licencing considerations. A program using an existing database (e.g. Microsoft Access) may
require that database software be installed on all computers, which would mean paying for licences. Custom software would not require this expense.

● Social and ethical considerations. The company should also consider aspects like accessibility for vision and mobility-impaired users. For example, accessibility features may be readily available in existing database software.

questions.title: Designing, Modelling, and Planning the Development and Deployment of a Visitor Check-In System (Question 26, ITE 2015)

items.text:
Green Mountain School has engaged Good Software, a software development company, to  build a new electronic visitor check-in system for the school. Good Software consists of a  small team of five developers who work on custom software projects for small to medium  businesses. It is a distributed team with the developers working from home in locations all  around the country. 

Currently when visitors arrive at the school they need to check-in by writing their details  into a visitor log book, and then be issued with a non-personalised visitors badge. 

With this new system, when a visitor arrives at school reception they will type their name  into a tablet computer, along with their email address and the staff member who they are  visiting (this field will autocomplete from the school’s staff database). If they have not  visited the school before they will be prompted to read and agree to the school’s evacuation  and lockdown policies – they only need to agree to the policies once, as the system will  remember if they have visited previously and already registered their agreement (using their  email address which is assumed to be unique to each visitor). The visitor’s details will be  stored in a database on the tablet along with the date and time of their check-in. Finally, a  name label for the visit will be printed on a connected label printer with their name. 

The system needs to be built within one month. Good Software intend to build the software  using a development environment called DatabasePro, a database application available for  the tablet device.
Draw a storyboard for this system.

Describes a suitable software development approach.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Rapid Application Development (RAD) would be the most suitable approach. RAD is suitable for
projects which are small-scale and need to be developed in a short time frame. These are both
requirements of Green Mountain School, since they are unlikely to be investing large amounts of
money in this project and also need it completed within one month. Additionally, RAD projects are
most often developed in 4th generation languages which allow for the fast development of software packages using visual design tools combined with existing libraries of code. Good Software have indicated that they will be building the system in DatabasePro which, from the name and brief description, appears to be a suitable development environment for the project and also for the RAD approach.


 The structured approach is not suitable given the small scale and small budget of this project.
It is also not complex enough to justify the rigid and prescriptive process of structured.


 Prototyping could be used as part of the user interface development, but given the simple
requirements of the project complex prototyping is not required.


 The agile approach could suit the time requirements for this project, but given this system
should not need to be iteratively improved (due to its simplicity) the agile approach is not the
most suitable.


 End user development is not suitable as the school does not have the in-house expertise to

questions.title: Design and Implementation of a Word-Guessing Game (Question 29, ITE 2022)

items.text:
A new game is being developed called Guess the Word. In this game the player has ten chances to guess a randomly selected five letter word.

  • A five character long hint string is returned after each incorrect guess.
  • If the player guesses a letter in the correct spot, the correct letter is returned in the hint.
  • If the player guesses a letter which is not in the word or is not in the correct spot a question mark “?” is returned in that location within the hint string.
  • Guesses that are not words do not count as a guess.

An example of a game is below, where the correct word was PLANE and it took the player four guesses to guess the word correctly.

 

Guess 1: APPLE

Hint: ????E

Guess 2: PELIE

Not a valid word

Guess 2: SLATE

Hint: ?LA?E

Guess 3: PLATE

Hint: PLA?E

Guess 4: PLANE

Got it in 4 guesses

 

An algorithm for the mainline of the game is as follows.

BEGIN GuessWord

wordsArray = ReadWordsFile

word = RandomWord(wordsArray)

chance = 1

REPEAT

guess = GetCheckGuess(chance)

hint = GenerateHint(guess, word)

Print “Hint: “ hint

Increment chance

UNTIL guess=word OR chance>10

IF guess=word THEN

Print “Got it in “ chance “ guesses”

ELSE

Print “No more chances – the word was “ word

ENDIF

END GuessWord

The GetCheckGuess subroutine gets and verifies each guess entered by the user is legitimate. Describe the essential processing tasks performed by this subroutine. You are not required to write the algorithm

criteria.criterion: Excellent description of the GetCheckGuess processing
Limited description of the GetCheckGuess processing

The routine then checks the guess is 5 characters long and then that it is a valid word found within the wordsArray. If the input is not valid then “Not a valid word” is displayed and the user is asked for another word.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
BEGIN ReadWordsFile

counter = 1

OPEN words.txt FOR INPUT

WHILE NOT end of file words.txt

READ word FROM words.txt

wordsArray[counter] = word

counter = counter + 1

END WHILE

CLOSE words.txt

RETURN wordsArray

END ReadWordsFile

items.text: Write an algorithm for the GenerateHint subroutine. You may assume a string can be accessed as an array, for example if word=”PLANE” then word(3)=”A”.

criteria.criterion: Correct structure chart including all subroutines, parameters and arrows
Substantially correct structure chart including most subroutines, parameters and arrows
Structure chart showing understanding of the relationship between the algorithm and the chart
Limited response showing sone understanding of structure charts

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
BEGIN GenerateHint(guess, word)

hint = “”

FOR i = 1 TO 5 STEP 1

IF guess(i) = word(i) THEN

hint(i) = word(i)

ELSE

hint(i) = “?”

ENDIF

NEXT i

RETURN hint

END GenerateHint

items.text:
An enhancement is planned so that correct letters that are not in the correct location within a guess are indicated as part of each hint. 

Recommend how such an enhancement could be implemented in terms of the output to the user and in terms of the processing required and its location within the algorithm.

criteria.criterion: Correct structure chart including all subroutines, parameters and arrows
Substantially correct structure chart including most subroutines, parameters and arrows
Structure chart showing understanding of the relationship between the algorithm and the chart
Limited response showing sone understanding of structure charts

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
This enhancement could be implemented by using the existing question marks “?” to indicate correct letters in wrong locations and maybe dashes “-“ to indicate completely incorrect letters. For example if Guess=APPLE and word=PLANE then the hint would be “-?-?E”.

Note that the processing must consider how to deal with multiple letters in a guess when the letter appears just once in the word. It will also be necessary to ensure that letters in the correct position are not considered should a duplicate of that letter appear elsewhere in the guess.

Considering the above difficulties, and simplifying the enhancement algorithm, it would likely be better to perform the current exact match processing in the existing GenerateHint subroutine first so that the new algorithm already knows of matches and can ignore them as it searches for matching letters in word.

This additional enhancement subroutine could be called PartialMatch implemented as a separate subroutine called from within the existing GenerateHint subroutine just prior to returning hint to the mainline or it could be called after the GenerateHint subroutine within the mainline GuessWord routine. In either case, PartialMatch will require access to hint, guess and word, whether directly or via passed parameters.
